html:
A Buddhist monastery built on a sheer cliff some 900 metres above the Paro valley in Bhutan. The main temple complex dates from 1692.

The site is holy because of Padmasambhava, or Guru Rinpoche, the 8th century teacher who helped bring Buddhism to Tibet and the Himalaya. Legend says he flew here on the back of a tigress and meditated in a cave on the cliff, subduing a local demon. "Taktsang" means tiger's lair.

The monastery was built by Tenzin Rabgye, ruler of Bhutan, in the generations after the Zhabdrung unified the country as a Buddhist state. It belongs to the Vajrayana tradition shared with Tibet. A fire in 1998 destroyed the main buildings; they were rebuilt by 2005. Reached by a long steep walk, it is now Bhutan's best known image and a goal for pilgrims and visitors alike.
sum: A Buddhist monastery built on a sheer cliff some 900 metres above the Paro valley in Bhutan. The main temple complex dates from 1692.
